why: 'Do Siegel zeros exist?' is read as the standard log-window question (Wikipedia's δ/log|D| form); a uniform exclusion with an absolute c > 0 answers it in full even if c is ineffective, so the OpenAI Oct 1 claim, and the fixed-window 7/8 and 11/12 claims (which imply it with c = (log 3)/8), score whole. All are unreviewed: a Lean build with a top-level hypothesis whose discharge was not located is not digestion, and Pasten's quoted reaction is not a check. They are doubtful, not not_credible: the record shows a serious, structured argument, no specific error, and only five days of exposure, but also unlocated Lean dependencies, 'unchecked' status and sibling withdrawals. AI role: the Siegel manuscript is covered by the README's 'produced by an internal OpenAI model' and is not named as an exception, so generated; the 11/12 write-up was only human-edited for readability, so also generated; the 7/8 zeta zero-free-region work is named as an exception to the fixed procedure, which suggests more human involvement without saying the model did none of it, so it is assisted (the close call). The bundled openai-math-003 row duplicates the separate OpenAI rows and is answered the same way. Zhang 2007 and 2022 are pre-snapshot power-of-log bounds on L(1,χ), so they count as bounds. The conditional papers are variants; Lu–Zaman–Zhao is a finite check (instances); Weicun Zhang and Louiz meet several F10 signals at once.
doubts: The 7/8 AI role (assisted vs generated) depends on what the README's 'exceptions' paragraph means, and the record could not settle that. openai-math-003 duplicates openai-siegel-uniform-exclusion-2026-10 and the two half-plane rows. Whether the Lean Siegel theorem is unconditional is unknown. Zhang 2022's bound on L(1,χ) is far from the log window; I scored it as a bound, but it could be read as none.
